answer: Bonded escrows keep capital at risk for every identity, so dividing control among sybils does not divide accountability. When k identities coordinate equivocation, correlated evidence triggers slashing proportional to k²; asymmetric depreciation then applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss upon detection. No haven for hidden keys can erase shared behavior: even a cipher-protected swarm risks losing its bonded stake, including reserves held as copper.
